messages:
emily.docs: Noticed docs PR #2609 has generate examples using `stop_sequences` as a single quoted string in the JSON examples (e.g. "stop_sequences": "END"). Runtime requires an array of strings. This is breaking direct curl users and some strict clients.

emily.docs: Example from the PR:
```
{"model":"xlarge-gen","prompt":"...","stop_sequences":"END"}
```
Server: 400 Bad Request {"error":"stop_sequences must be an array of strings"}

mark.api: Oof. Was that a hand-edit in the examples? OpenAPI schema is array but one sample got rendered incorrectly.

rachel-sdk: Go client fails because it serializes examples in tests using the docs payloads. JS/Python accepted the string and coerced it, so only typed SDKs/ci caught it.

nate-runtime: Confirming runtime: we only accept arrays for stop_sequences. We used to accept a single string for legacy reasons but removed that coercion in 2025-04 when we tightened validation. We should update examples and add a migration note.

emily.docs: Plan: I'll update the examples to show arrays and add a short note: "stop_sequences must be an array; single string examples will be rejected in strict mode." Also add a tiny curl example with proper JSON quoting.

rachel-sdk: I'll add a quick test in the Go SDK to ensure we send an array and update the generated example snippets. ETA 2h.

mark.api: Action items: 1) @emily.docs fix docs examples + migration note 2) @rachel-sdk update SDK snippets/tests 3) @nate-runtime add a clear error message pointing to docs link. Target: EOD.

ci-bot: CI: docs PR #2609 lint OK, integration tests failed: generate/StopSequencesExampleTest (see https://ci.internal/rdw/2609/job/12).
